title: Yochanan Chakuka’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.13a.11): he came before Rabbi to ask about a bag full of chametz that someone had deposited with him and that mice had pierced, etc. In the Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakhah 4, the incident is told as follows: a man deposited a bag of chametz with R. Ch. Rabbah; R. Y. bar Bun said, ‘It was Yochanan Chakukya.’ And in Bava Metzia, chapter 3, halakhah 4: Rabbi Yochanan Chakukah deposited chametz with R. Ch. Rubba; he asked Rabbi, etc.[^1]

Pesachim 53b relates that he once went out to the villages. They asked him whether the wheat had done well, and he answered that the barley had done well. The reply was, ‘Go and bring the good news to the horses and donkeys.’ There R. Ch. explains that he was a scribe, while R. Y. explains that he was from the town of Chakukah.[^2]

notes.text: The name occurs as חקוקאה, חקוקיא, and חקוקה, with the epithets רבה and רובא also differing. The personal initials ר״ח and ר״י are ambiguous. Hyman’s two Yerushalmi accounts give different depositors and recipients.

The initials R. Ch. and R. Y. in the final paragraph refer to commentators and need not identify the people in the earlier accounts. Hyman does not name the speaker of the reply about horses and donkeys.
